MU.thesis: Micron sits at the center of a multi-year, supply-constrained HBM/DRAM AI super-cycle with sold-out 2026-27 capacity, record pricing power, and repeated blow-out earnings that are driving aggressive upward estimate and price-target revisions.
red_flags: Hyperscaler customer concentration (Microsoft, Meta, Amazon, Google, Oracle)
Historical memory-industry cyclicality and risk of supply overshoot
China exposure/geopolitical export-control risk
Elevated expectations bar after 700%+ 1-year stock run
catalysts: HBM4 ramp tied to Nvidia Vera Rubin platform
Fiscal Q4 2026 earnings (~$50B revenue guide)
New capacity coming online in Idaho, NY, Japan, Singapore, India
Further multi-year fixed-price HBM supply agreements with hyperscalers

WDC.thesis: WDC is riding a supply-constrained, multi-year AI-driven HDD upcycle with sold-out capacity through 2028, pricing power, and broad upward estimate revisions, though the stock has already run massively and trades near/above consensus targets.
red_flags: customer concentration in top 7 hyperscalers
stock up ~785% YoY, valuation stretched vs targets
GAAP earnings inflated by one-time non-cash Sandisk gain
Kioxia merger talks add strategic uncertainty
insider selling activity noted
catalysts: Aug 5, 2026 Q4 FY26 earnings
HAMR/30TB+ drive qualification progress
new hyperscaler contract extensions into 2028-2029
potential Kioxia deal resolution

STX.thesis: Seagate's HAMR/Mozaic ramp is unlocking a multi-year AI-driven HDD upcycle with sold-out capacity through 2027, oligopoly pricing power, and the steepest estimate revisions in the group, though valuation and insider selling warrant sizing discipline.
red_flags: heavy insider selling (~$108-113M in 3 months)
customer/hyperscaler concentration
stretched valuation (P/E ~64-84x)
lead independent director retiring Oct 2026
catalysts: FQ4/FY2026 earnings July 28, 2026
Mozaic 4+ becoming majority of HAMR exabyte shipments by end-2026
2027 nearline capacity contract negotiations/pricing
Mozaic 5 qualification shipments late 2027

STRL.thesis: Sterling is riding a still-accelerating data-center/semiconductor mission-critical infrastructure build-out with record backlog, repeated guidance raises, and the strongest estimate-revision momentum in the grid/power-infra peer set, though rich valuation and insider selling warrant position sizing discipline.
red_flags: Heavy CEO/insider selling ($22.7M+ recent CEO sale, $27.1M insiders over 3 months)
Customer/end-market concentration in data center & semiconductor mega-projects
New S-3 shelf registration signals potential future dilution
Valuation already prices in aggressive growth (P/E ~63x vs peers ~41x)
Execution/integration risk from CEC acquisition and capacity constraints (labor/PMs)
catalysts: Q2 2026 earnings report (Aug 10, 2026)
Additional large semiconductor/data-center contract wins
Further FY26 guidance raises
Backlog conversion and CEC margin improvement (300-500bps target)
Continued bolt-on M&A in mission-critical infrastructure

NVT.thesis: NVT is riding an accelerating, multi-year AI data-center and grid-modernization capex cycle with a $2.6B backlog into 2027, product-led share gains, and sharply rising analyst estimates, though it carries data-center concentration and input-cost risk.
red_flags: Heavy reliance on AI/data-center capex cycle sustaining demand
Copper/tariff inflation pressuring Electrical Connections margins
New CSCO hire (Mar 2026) still ramping - key-person/execution risk
Valuation has re-rated sharply, raising bar for continued beats
catalysts: Q2 2026 earnings (~late July 2026) and potential further guidance raise
Continued backlog-to-revenue conversion through 2026-2027
New product launches from Blaine, MN facility ramp
Additional hyperscaler liquid-cooling and power-utility order wins

MYRG.thesis: MYRG is a clean, low-leverage share-gainer riding the early innings of grid/T&D and data-center electrification capex, but the stock has already repriced hard and valuation, not fundamentals, is now the main risk.
red_flags: Stock up 136% YoY with rich valuation multiple (~35x future P/E) leaving little margin for error
Wide analyst target dispersion ($153-$564) signals high uncertainty on durability of grid demand
Customer concentration typical of utility/EPC contract model
High-voltage transmission award catalyst not yet materialized, pushing next growth leg to FY27-28
catalysts: Q2 2026 earnings July 29, 2026
Potential large high-voltage (345/500/765kV) transmission contract awards
Continued data center-driven C&I demand
Further backlog records supporting 2027-2028 revenue visibility
Opportunistic M&A and prefab capacity expansion

CGNX.thesis: Cognex is at the start of an AI-vision platform cycle (OneVision, NVIDIA/Qualcomm-powered In-Sight lines) driving accelerating estimate revisions and share gains in a growing machine-vision TAM, though rich valuation and heavy insider selling warrant caution.
red_flags: Elevated valuation (~75-78x trailing earnings)
Significant recent insider selling by VPs (~$9.3M and $1.3M sales)
CEO succession/key-person risk disclosed in filings
Customer concentration risk in logistics/auto/consumer electronics
Tariff-related gross margin drag
catalysts: Q2 2026 earnings Aug 5, 2026 (guidance already raised well above Street)
OneVision platform scaling from pilot to multi-site enterprise rollouts
Continued AI-vision hardware refresh cycle (In-Sight 6900/3900) driving upgrade demand
Logistics vertical double-digit growth streak extending
Further sell-side estimate/price-target upgrades post beat-and-raise pattern

OUST.thesis: Ouster is entering a new Rev8/Physical-AI product cycle with expanding multi-vertical TAM and a regulatory tailwind from Hesai's US exclusion, but dilution and lumpy losses temper conviction.
red_flags: Recent $192M dilutive equity offering at a discount, closely following a May 2026 raise
Insider selling ~$36.3M over trailing 3 months
GAAP net losses persist ($17.5M in Q1'26) with volatile gross margin (60% to 43% QoQ)
Revenue lumpiness tied to large/customer-concentrated deals
catalysts: Rev8 ramp to >100k units/year via Benchmark partnership
NVIDIA DRIVE Hyperion qualification driving auto adoption
Defense/counter-UAS and BABA-compliant infrastructure wins (BlueCity, ARGUS)
Q2 2026 earnings (Aug 6) and further Rev8 design-win disclosures

TER.thesis: Teradyne is riding a genuine new-product-driven AI test and physical-AI robotics cycle with expanding TAM, share gains, and broad-based analyst upgrades, though customer concentration and stretched valuation temper the risk/reward.
red_flags: customer concentration (5 customers = 44% of 2025 revenue)
AI capex/hyperscaler dependency (~70% of revenue AI-linked)
lumpy order timing causing guidance volatility
rich valuation (~40x+ forward EBITDA) vs. Street mean target
robotics unit restructuring/layoffs
cybersecurity attack attempts disclosed
catalysts: Q2 2026 earnings July 28
merchant GPU multisystem production ramp
silicon photonics (Photon 100) and Omnyx board-test ramp
HBM/memory test demand from hyperscaler capex
physical AI robotics rollout (MiR1200, UR AI Trainer, PolyScope X)

HWM.thesis: HWM is a top-5 oligopoly supplier riding a synchronized commercial aero build-rate, spares, defense, and data-center-driven IGT upcycle with consistent guidance raises and broad Street estimate upgrades, though valuation is now demanding.
red_flags: 40x EV/EBITDA valuation looks stretched vs history
insiders net sellers (~$25M last 12 months, incl. large recent EVP sale)
customer concentration in commercial OEM/engine programs
share price has outrun EPS growth (80%/yr vs 40%/yr over 3 years)
catalysts: Q2 2026 earnings Aug 6, 2026 with FY26 EPS guided to $4.88-$5.00
Continued IGT capacity expansion tied to data center power demand
Integration of CAM and Brunner acquisitions expanding fastener/structures capacity
Rising defense modernization and titanium/aero-structure demand (8.6% CAGR TAM)

HEI.thesis: HEICO is compounding through an accelerating niche-acquisition strategy in aerospace/defense MRO and electronics, backed by broad analyst estimate upgrades, but trades at a rich multiple with rising leverage funding the deal engine.
red_flags: Forward P/E ~58x vs industrials avg ~21x, flagged as overvalued
$1.2B senior notes raised and credit facility expanded to $2.2B to fund M&A, increasing leverage
Electronic Technologies segment margins volatile quarter to quarter (19.8% to 26.5%)
Growth model heavily reliant on continuous bolt-on acquisitions rather than pure organic pricing power
Recent insider stock sale by a top executive
catalysts: Continued bolt-on M&A (Sherwood Avionics, Southwest Antennas, Cook Defence) expanding defense/MRO footprint
Strong backlog and record FY2026 guidance ($5.78 EPS, +18% YoY)
Rising PMA adoption discussions amid airline cost pressures
Sustained defense demand for missiles/munitions and mission-critical electronics

GE.thesis: GE Aerospace's dominant installed base and $210B+ backlog drive durable, estimate-beating growth, but a 40-46x valuation and moderating order growth cap near-term upside despite genuine early-stage defense-propulsion optionality.
red_flags: Operating margin down 130bps YoY on inflation/investment costs
Spare parts delinquencies up 20% sequentially, supply chain constrained
Rich valuation (~40-46x forward EPS) leaves little room for error
Insider sales only (6 sells, 0 buys) in past 12 months
GE9X losses expected to persist until 2028
catalysts: Continued LEAP/GE9X delivery ramp and durability kit rollout (2027 cutover)
New defense engine program wins (XA102, GE426, F404 exports)
Further guidance raises if commercial services backlog conversion accelerates
Easing supply-chain/spare-parts constraints boosting delivery cadence

GH.thesis: Guardant is compounding through a genuine, multi-front product cycle (Shield screening + Guardant360 CDx expansion) with accelerating volumes, repeated beat-and-raise guidance, and broadening reimbursement, though funded by heavy dilution and against emerging Freenome/Exact/Abbott competition in colorectal screening.
red_flags: Persistent net losses and stockholders' deficit (~$181M)
$1.5B in convertible notes with ongoing equity/convert issuance and dilution risk
Intensifying colorectal screening competition (Freenome/Exact Sciences, Abbott)
Pending patent litigation ($83.4M adverse verdict under appeal)
catalysts: Q2 2026 earnings July 30, 2026 with Shield volume update
USPSTF colorectal screening guideline update expected in 2026
Potential FDA approval/expansion of Shield 2.0 and additional CDx label expansions
Camizestrant FDA approval as incremental Guardant360 upside not yet in guidance

LLY.thesis: Lilly is compounding through a rare double product cycle—still-scaling injectable GLP-1 dominance plus a newly launched oral pill—while estimates and price targets keep rising.
red_flags: High revenue concentration in Mounjaro/Zepbound (~65% of sales)
Ongoing realized-price erosion from cash-pay cuts and government pricing deal
Intensifying oral GLP-1 competition from Novo Nordisk and emerging entrants
Large pre-launch inventory build creates write-off risk if uptake disappoints
Mid-2030s patent cliff on core metabolic franchise
catalysts: Orforglipron/Foundayo oral pill commercial ramp and diabetes indication filing
Retatrutide Phase 3 readouts and eventual launch
Continued international volume expansion (China NRDL, ex-US markets)
Zepbound label expansion into adjacent indications (sleep apnea, psoriasis combo)
Q2 2026 earnings on Aug 5

NTRA.thesis: Natera is compounding through a broadening MRD/oncology and prenatal franchise with guideline tailwinds, international expansion, and a new average-risk screening TAM opening up, though heavy insider selling and slowing forward growth warrant some caution.
red_flags: Persistent insider selling by CEO, Executive Chairman, and directors ($85M+ recently)
Still unprofitable with EPS misses
Rising competition from Guardant Reveal/Shield, Exact Sciences, Roche-SAGA
Consensus expects revenue growth deceleration vs historical trend
catalysts: Japan Signatera commercial launch (end of 2026)
FIND-CRC/PROCEED-CRC average-risk screening data and potential FDA filing
Additional NCCN guideline inclusions (bladder, other cancers)
EU IVDR Class C certification enabling broader European expansion
Q2 2026 earnings report (7/30/2026)

GEV.thesis: GEV is the picks-and-shovels play on AI-driven electricity demand with a record $176B backlog, pricing power in capacity-constrained gas turbines, and accelerating grid/electrification orders, though Wind losses and stretched valuation are real offsets.
red_flags: Wind segment persistent EBITDA losses (~$275M/qtr) and offshore litigation (Vineyard Wind)
Earnings quality diluted by ~$4.4B one-time Prolec GE remeasurement gain
Q2 adjusted EPS missed consensus by ~19%
Stretched valuation (P/E ~31-59x, flagged as overvalued)
Rising customer concentration around hyperscaler/data-center capex cycle
Tariff cost exposure ($100-200M in 2026)
catalysts: Year-end 2026 gas turbine backlog update (guided to 125+ GW)
Continued data-center order momentum in Electrification segment
Progress toward 2028/2030 turbine capacity expansion targets
Resolution of offshore wind litigation/claims
Q3 2026 earnings (early Nov) for margin trajectory confirmation

PLTR.thesis: Palantir's AI platform is compounding at 85%+ revenue growth with expanding margins and deep government/defense moats, but a stretched valuation, heavy insider selling, and UK contract scrutiny are driving multiple compression that has broken the stock's trend despite improving fundamentals.
red_flags: Sustained insider selling by Karp, CTO Sankar, and directors flagged as a negative confidence signal
Government/customer revenue concentration (~54-55% of revenue)
UK NHS contract under full parliamentary review amid data-sovereignty conflict with US CLOUD Act
Valuation at ~60-90x forward sales/earnings leaves no room for execution missteps
Founder voting-trust structure concentrates control risk
catalysts: Q2 2026 earnings report Aug 3, 2026 (9th straight beat-and-raise potential)
Continued AIP/commercial expansion beyond US (currently 133% US commercial growth)
New sovereign AI deals (NVIDIA partnership) and defense standardization (Army NGC2 on Foundry)
Resolution/clarity on NHS Federated Data Platform review reducing UK political overhang

UBER.thesis: Uber's core platform economics (margin inflection, Uber One flywheel) remain strong, but decelerating growth, broken relative-strength trend, and rising Waymo/AV disintermediation risk keep this a show-me story rather than a confirmed outlier winner.
red_flags: Waymo exiting shared markets (Phoenix ended, Austin/Atlanta exit planned by 2028)
GAAP earnings volatility from equity-investment revaluations
Continued SBC dilution requiring offsetting buybacks
Net insider selling over trailing 12 months
26-week relative strength -30% vs theme ETF, trend not intact
catalysts: Aug 5 2026 Q2 earnings/guidance update
Scaling of Nuro/Lucid, Rivian, Wayve/Nissan robotaxi deployments through 2027-2028
Uber One membership growth beyond 50M and rising penetration of Gross Bookings
$20B buyback execution reducing share count
Resolution/renewal of AV partner terms in contested markets (Austin, Atlanta)
